review: The hymn is the soul's converse with its Beloved: 1:1–8 is Ps 73:23–26 with John 14:6 and 1 Pet 2:24, 2:1–8 is Ps 16:5–6 with Ps 119:35, and 3:1–8 is Ps 27:4 (אַחַת שָׁאַלְתִּי) with Ps 16:8.

The last line of each stanza is longer and ends with the vocative דּוֹדִי, exactly as the print ends every stanza with يَا حَبِيبِي; the payload keeps the longer line rather than trimming the address.

3:5–6 אַחַת אֲבַקֵּשׁ … לִרְאוֹתְךָ בִּצְדִּי — the Arabic وَاحِدًا أَرْجُوهُ … أَنْ أَرَاكَ بِجِوَارِي is the psalm's 'one thing' petition; the Hebrew keeps אַחַת of Ps 27:4 and the concrete 'at my side', so the request is the psalmist's and not a general wish.
